pr_title: Remove option ot set a task instance to running state in UI
pr_body:
Removes the "Set to state 'running'" option from UI for Task instances. If users are using this, immediately an "Zombie task" error like the following is produced in the task logs:
```
[2023-12-31, 18:57:01 CET] {scheduler_job_runner.py:1766} ERROR - Detected zombie job: {'full_filepath': '/opt/airflow/airflow/example_dags/example_params_ui_tutorial.py', 'processor_subdir': '/files/dags', 'msg': "{'DAG Id': 'example_params_ui_tutorial', 'Task Id': 'show_params', 'Run Id': 'manual__2023-12-31T18:56:01+01:00', 'Hostname': 'c01bb381ee62', 'External Executor Id': '0464fee6-8ba2-4a3b-87cc-f9c0d891bfa9'}", 'simple_task_instance': <airflow.models.taskinstance.SimpleTaskInstance object at 0x7f8ac6c4b6a0>, 'is_failure_callback': True} (See https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/core-concepts/tasks.html#zombie-undead-tasks)
```
See also https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/core-concepts/tasks.html#zombie-undead-tasks

Reason for removal is that the setting to state "running" just creates an inconsistent state in the meta database, no background activity is started. For advanced user who know what they are doing, rather the API `HTTP PATCH /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}' is the right way. But we should not leave a standard option in the normal user UI as this is mis-leading.

closes: #35729

issue_context.title: Setting a task to run state doesn't do nothing
issue_context.body:
### Apache Airflow version

Other Airflow 2 version (please specify below)

### What happened

If I set the task to running here, it goes to the "running" state but does nothing
![image](https://github.com/apache/airflow/assets/19591174/20d1fefd-15a1-4020-8f50-c8561f608e53)



### What you think should happen instead

I think the option should be removed for **tasks**

### How to reproduce

Set a queued task to running state

### Operating System

Airflow 2.7.2 Python3.10 official image

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

_No response_

### Deployment

Official Apache Airflow Helm Chart

### Deployment details

_No response_

### Anything else

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit PR?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
comments:
I think this setting of state is an administrative "overright" of the original status and can be used in any kind of troubleshooting - but you need to know what you are doing. It is not intended to use it to (re-)launch tasks. It plainly sets the state,

In my job I used all of the other states and on this point I agree - I am not sure how useful it is to set a task to "running". If it is running it should have received this status, it the task is not running and is not started (it will not with this action) then it is never turned to any follow-up state,

I would leave the judgement to others with a bit more legacy on the UI but I assume it would really make sense to remove or print three warnings for the option.

review_comments: I agree with you on the removal of this feature. However, what is the case for which we have introduced this? Don't we want to mark this as deprecated before deleting this?

Thanks for the comments. I tried to trace-back in GIT the history and the "oldest" lines in the removed code were 6+ years ago added. But in a case of UI re-factoring. Most of the other lines were re-factored multiple times since beginning. Could not find any traces in Release Notes on this. But history goes back to early 1.10 releases (1.10.2) in Jan 2019.

I believe at this time the concepts of Airflow were totally different, schedulers behaved also different in many details. I would also believe there might have been a use case in the past. But I was thinking hard and can not imagine a use case where this option is bringing any benefit (in contrast to users mis-lead by thinking they can really trigger a start manually).

I also thought multiple times about this bug report and nobody responded. So I believe this option is actually of no-use. But I am happy if somebody convinces me of a use case where this option is beneficial.

I would not deprecate it if it is of no use. If there is a real use of this function I'd rather keep it with a confirmation/warning dialog.

I would consider this as a bugfix and hence no need of deprecation perhaps. Just setting a taskinstance as running but there being no corresponding active job for it would be the reason for it becoming a zombie.

I believe the web UI component we don't consider as a public interface so should be ok to remove https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/public-airflow-interface.html#what-is-not-part-of-the-public-interface-of-apache-airflow
Yes I agree. This is a bug fix no need for any deprecation notice
